```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%", dev = "svglite", fig.ext = "svg",
  dev.args = list(pointsize = 14))
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 17) + theme(
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
  legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
  legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
  legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA)))
```

An ordination places observations on a small set of axes computed from their measured variables. A biplot draws the observations and variable directions in the same view. `stat_biplot_3d()` composes site points, solid-headed quiver arrows and optional group regions.

```{r iris}
fit <- prcomp(iris[1:4], scale. = TRUE)
groups <- setNames(iris$Species, rownames(iris))
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(fit, groups = groups, region = "ellipsoid",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

For `prcomp`, sites use `fit$x` and arrows use `fit$rotation`. `loading_scale` explicitly multiplies the arrow vectors for display. The chosen multiplier therefore belongs in a figure's methods or caption. `choices` selects the three axes.

Site identifiers are the score matrix's row names, or sequential character identifiers when row names are absent. Group membership is joined by these identifiers. A named vector or a table with `id` and `group` columns can supply membership in any order.

```{r hull}
membership <- data.frame(id = names(groups), group = unname(groups))
membership <- membership[rev(seq_len(nrow(membership))), ]
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(fit, groups = membership, region = "hull",
                        loading_scale = 2, label_size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

## Vegan scores

[vegan](https://vegandevs.github.io/vegan/) supplies ecological ordination methods and a `scores()` generic that applies their scaling conventions. `stat_biplot_3d()` calls that generic for vegan fits. Pass method-specific arguments in `scores_args`, or supply a list containing `sites` and `species` score matrices directly.

```{r vegan, eval=requireNamespace("vegan", quietly=TRUE)}
model <- vegan::rda(iris[1:4], scale = TRUE)
ggplot() + stat_biplot_3d(model, groups = groups,
                        scores_args = list(scaling = 2), label_size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

The group ellipsoids use `stat_ellipsoid_3d(type = "norm")`. Their level describes the spread of observations under that covariance model. Individual point, quiver, text, hull and ellipsoid layers can also be composed directly when a figure needs separate mappings. [vegan3d](https://rdrr.io/cran/vegan3d/man/vegan3d-package.html) documents the corresponding ordination and group-region conventions.
